title: The scalar tensor quotient comparison commutes with normalized reduction
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D, a prime l≠D.p, finite extensions E,L of Q_l, an embedding iota:E→L, a scheme X, a derived complete integral E-complex K and n≤m. Let T be the completed scalar extension and Q_i:r_(L,i)(TK)≅T_(iota_i)(r_(E,i)K) the prescribed quotient comparison of [def-sf-integral-finite-extension-models]. Write d_F for the normalized reduction transition of [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] and a for [def-sf-scalar-reduction-exchange]. Then Q_m;T_(iota_m)(d_E(K));a_(r_(E,n)K)=d_L(TK);Res_L(Q_n). This assertion is about every complete K and does not involve a dualizing datum or a finite exceptional counit.

proof.text: Conjugate by completion and use naturality of normalized reduction transitions to move the completion maps to the same side. Expand the remaining quotient comparison into finiteReductionIso and tensorSquare.

Transpose under the target scalar adjunction at m. The mixed comparison is the mate of the section-normalized restriction square. The two leftAdjointUniq comparisons in tensorSquare and finiteReductionIso preserve precisely these units. Both transposes therefore send x to 1 tensor x at level n; the two pasted restriction maps are identity on sections. Sheafification and localization preserve this equality, and Hom adjunction injectivity gives the displayed square.

theorem quotient_reduction_transition
    (K : IntegralVerdier.Ambient l E X) (hK : IsSfDerivedComplete l E X K)
    {m n : ℕ} (h : n ≤ m) :
    (quotient l E L ι X m K hK).hom ≫
        (pbcDerivedExtend (integralScalarQuotientSheafMap l E L ι X m)).map
          (normalizedDVRReductionTransition l E X D hl h K) ≫
        (scalarReductionExchange l E L ι X h).app
          ((scalarReductionDerivedExtension l E X n).obj K) =
      normalizedDVRReductionTransition l L X D hl h
          ((integralScalarExtensionOfUniverses l E L ι X).obj K) ≫
        (normalizedDVRRes l L X h).map (quotient l E L ι X n K hK).hom
